clue.text: Put out about lines presented by shop discounting soft toy

indicators.note: about means the word for put out goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

indicators.note: discounting means leaving out, so the letter for soft is dropped from shop

parts.note: taken as the word itself
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper snubbing a cuddly toy makes someone put out about the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft toy' looks like a teddy bear, but 'soft' is just the musical letter to drop and 'toy' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A doll's house is a miniature dwelling made as a plaything for children.

clue.text: Father and daughter upset about British ruins

indicators.note: about means the reversed pieces wrap around the letter for British
upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A father and daughter are distressed by the state of some ruined British building.
explanation.walkthrough: SIRE + D reversed gives DERIS, and B goes inside after DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains left after something is destroyed, which is what ruins are.

clue.text: Left cathedral site after working without support?

indicators.note: after places the cathedral city at the end

parts.note: ON means working, as a machine that is on
Ely is a small English city famous for its cathedral

explanation.surface: Someone left a cathedral town after a job and had nobody to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England. The question mark flags that 'without support' is a loose way of saying friendless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lonely lacks companions to back them up, so they are alone and unsupported.

clue.text: What environmentalists note we don't have? It's only to be expected

definitions.text: What environmentalists note we don't have?
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: we have only one natural world, no spare or second one
second meaning: behaviour that comes automatically, so it is just what you would expect

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: green campaigners warn that there is no replacement planet, no 'second nature'.
explanation.definitionFit: Second nature means a habit so ingrained that it happens automatically, so it is predictable.

clue.text: Take top off protective cover smeared in grease?

indicators.note: take top off means the first letter, the top in a down clue, is removed

parts.note: a doily is a small mat laid under dishes to protect a surface

explanation.surface: An instruction to peel a smeared protective covering off something greasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in grease is greasy, and the word for that is a synonym of slick.

clue.text: Observed point about acceptable speech taking a convoluted tack

indicators.note: about means the observed-plus-point pair goes round the speech abbreviation

parts.note: seen means observed
RP, Received Pronunciation, is the standard accent of British English
a tine is a point, as on a fork or antler

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a talk which sounded proper actually wandered around the point.
explanation.walkthrough: Received Pronunciation is the standard accent of educated southern British English, hence 'acceptable speech'.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine means winding like a snake, so a serpentine path twists and turns.

clue.text: One keeps working banking system in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: BACS is the UK's automated system for bank payments

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their job at a bank during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS is the British clearing system for direct debits and salaries. 'Recession' looks economic but means backing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a strikebreaker, a worker who carries on during a strike.

clue.text: Sound of surprise about doctor bandaging male soldier

indicators.note: about means the sound of surprise goes round everything else

parts.note: coo is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping, so the doctor's letters wrap round the male

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
man means a male

explanation.surface: Someone gasps as a medic dresses a wounded soldier's injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo' is a mainly British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids as part of an elite unit.

clue.text: Mate correct about hospital booklet

parts.note: bro, short for brother, is a mate

indicators.note: about means the word for correct goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: to cure is to put right, to correct

explanation.surface: A friend fixes a hospital information leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: A brochure is a small printed pamphlet giving information or advertising.

clue.text: Set of viewers prohibits receiving half of vaccinations

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the word for prohibits contains the other piece

parts.note: bars means prohibits

indicators.note: half of means only the first six of the twelve letters are kept

parts.note: inoculations are vaccinations

explanation.surface: An authority bans part of a vaccination programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewers' suggests people watching, but here they are lenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Binoculars are a pair of linked lenses, one for each eye, so a matched set of viewing tubes.

clue.text: Target I eliminated before second round?

indicators.note: before puts the shortened target in front of the second
eliminated means the letter I is taken out of the word for target

parts.note: to aim at something is to target it
mo is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: A boxer says they took out their target before the second round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a boxing round but is a single bullet or shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo, short for ammunition, is what a round of firing is made of; a round is one cartridge.

clue.text: Standard border in church's interior design component

parts.note: a regiment's colours are its standard, its flag

indicators.note: in means the border sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A flag border features in the decor of a church interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church's interior' looks like one idea, but the apostrophe-s is just a link and HEM goes into CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour scheme is the chosen combination of colours, one part of an overall interior design.

clue.text: Article in papers about Holland away from the coast

indicators.note: in means the article is placed inside the papers abbreviation
about means the papers abbreviation also goes round the Holland code

parts.note: ID, identity papers
NL is the international code for the Netherlands, often called Holland
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the Netherlands describes an area remote from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: NL is the international vehicle code for the Netherlands, often loosely called Holland.
explanation.definitionFit: Inland means in the interior of a country, distant from the shore.

clue.text: Hard to follow revolutionary mood enshrined in top monument

indicators.note: to follow puts the hard letter after everything else
enshrined in means held inside, so the reversed mood goes within the word for top

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for mood is read backwards

parts.note: tone means mood or atmosphere
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A revolutionary spirit is enshrined in a great memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hard is the pencil-grade convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a war memorial honouring the dead who are buried elsewhere.

clue.text: Stomach upset, swallowing dodgy hooch? One can't keep away from bars

definitions.text: One can't keep away from bars

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the stomach upset contains the other letters

parts.note: colic is a severe pain in the stomach

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a bad stomach after drinking dubious bootleg spirits is a regular at bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs, but they are chocolate bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocoholic is someone addicted to chocolate, whose bars they cannot resist.

clue.text: I've had limited success on housing couple in English block

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the word for block holds the couple

parts.note: to hinder is to block
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A modest admission of only partial success when building homes for a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken in the first person, as the act itself might say it.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-hit wonder is an act known for a single successful record, so its success was confined to one.

clue.text: Fellow, one about to receive foremost of medals?

definitions.text: Fellow, one about to receive foremost of medals?

indicators.note: to receive means the word for fellow takes in the letter picked from medals

parts.note: chap means fellow

indicators.note: foremost of means the first letter of medals

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A man stands poised to collect the top medal.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes into CHAP to make CHAMP, followed by I and ON. The whole clue also describes the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the winner of a contest, the person who collects the gold medal.

clue.text: Want to fly with a shrill cry? This bird will do

indicators.note: to fly suggests scattering about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a yowl is a loud wailing cry

explanation.surface: A bird that wants to take off with a screech will fit the description.
explanation.walkthrough: WANT rearranged gives TAWN; 'with' joins it to YOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: The tawny owl is a common brown European owl known for its hooting calls.

clue.text: Husband getting care, then let out for community support?

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters of care, then and let are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband receives care and is then discharged into the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' reads as one phrase, but only 'out' is the signal and 'let' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A health centre is a local clinic, a place providing medical services to a neighbourhood.

clue.text: Material in petition in support of parent

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the petition comes after the parent

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, a parent
to ask is to petition

explanation.surface: Fabric features in a request supporting a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a rich patterned fabric, typically silk or linen, woven with reversible designs.

clue.text: Disreputable Observer article from the past presented in volume for us

indicators.note: presented in means placed inside, so the old article goes within the other letters

parts.note: our means belonging to us
ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: Reads like a review of a scandalous issue of a newspaper called The Observer, bound in a volume for readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the newspaper's name, but it is just one who watches. 'For' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyeur is a peeping Tom, someone who gets gratification from secretly watching others.

clue.text: Rulers prepared to participate in demo before end of day

indicators.note: before puts the march ahead of the last letter
to participate in means joining inside, so the word for prepared goes within the demo

parts.note: a march is a demonstration
on means ready or game, as in 'you're on'

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of day

explanation.surface: Rulers are getting ready to join a protest before the day ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a royal family or ruling dynasty, a collective term for those who reign.

clue.text: A lot of notes presented by old book

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an octave is a run of eight musical notes

explanation.surface: Many notes come from an old book.
explanation.definitionFit: An octavo is a book whose pages come from sheets folded into eight leaves.

clue.text: Uncertain state that's ignored over border

indicators.note: that's ignored means left out, so the letter for over is removed

parts.note: limbo is a state of uncertainty
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An unsettled situation over a frontier is being disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy and botany a limb is the edge or margin, such as the rim of the sun's disc.

clue.text: Unrelenting satirical attitude not carried through?

indicators.note: not carried through means unfinished, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: irony is a mocking, satirical stance

explanation.surface: A relentlessly sarcastic stance that never gets followed through.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron, as in an iron will, describes something firm and unyielding.

clue.text: Wrong speed — holding it to end of race, unable to understand the instructions?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the wrong-and-speed pair holds the other letters

parts.note: ill means wrong, as in ill-advised
rate means speed

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of race

explanation.surface: A runner going wrongly fast tries to keep it up to the finish and cannot follow the course directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a description of someone who cannot read written instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot read is unable to follow written directions, so they lack literacy.

clue.text: Irritation, dropping goods in river

indicators.note: dropping means losing, so the letters for goods are taken out

parts.note: a niggle is a small irritation
G is good, so GG is goods

explanation.surface: An annoyance about dumping cargo into a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great African river flowing north through Egypt.

clue.text: Conversation starter: "How to freeze a wave"

parts.note: to ice is to freeze
a breaker is a wave that breaks on the shore

explanation.surface: A chat-opener offered as a playful recipe for turning surf solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to' is a link; 'freeze a wave' reads as ice on a breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a remark or game used to ease tension when strangers first meet.
